rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā reports that Joseph's aunt hid Isaac's inherited prophetic belt on him and accused him of theft to keep him with her.
rows.anchor: قال قال الرضا عليه السلام في قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph broke his maternal grandfather's gold-and-silver idol and left it on the road, which his brothers later used to taunt him.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī considers the aunt-and-belt report more reliable than the report that Joseph stole an idol.
rows.anchor: أقول والرواية السابقة أقرب إلى الاعتماد

rows.speaker: يوسف عليه السلام
rows.claim: Other reports support the belt account: Joseph tells a prison guard not to love him, since his aunt's love led to a theft accusation, his father's love to his brothers' envy, and the woman's love to prison.
rows.anchor: إن السجان قال ليوسف إني لأحبك فقال لا تحبني فإن عمتى أحبتني

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph's excellence included making room for people, borrowing for the needy, and helping the weak.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { إنا نراك من المحسنين } قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Beautiful patience means not complaining to any person; Jacob's sole complaint was to God, as in 12:86.
rows.anchor: قال ذلك صبر ليس فيه شكوى إلى أحد من الناس إن إبراهيم بعث يعقوب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says that whoever publicly discloses grief has not been patient, and cites Jacob's complaint to God; another route reports it from Ibn ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: عن مسلم بن يسار يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jacob knew Joseph was alive because the Angel of Death said Joseph's soul had never passed to him; a variant says souls are taken singly and presented together.
rows.anchor: عن حنان بن سدير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قلت له أخبرني عن قول يعقوب لبنيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that Gabriel brought Jacob God's greeting and hope of reunion, and explained his blindness, bent back, and sons' treatment by a fasted beggar going unfed after a sheep was slaughtered.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وفيه أتى جبريل فقال يا يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the reported rebuke, Jacob regularly invited poor people to meals and invited poor fasters to break their fast with him.
rows.anchor: فكان يعقوب عليه السلام إذا أراد الغداء أمر مناديا ينادي ألا من أراد الغداء

rows.speaker: الله سبحانه
rows.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says God swore to return Jacob's sons after Jacob entrusted them to Him.
rows.anchor: ورد في الخبر إن الله سبحانه قال فبعزتي لأردنهما إليك من بعد ما توكلت علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's order completes the story: the shirt will restore his father's sight after grief and weeping blinded him.
rows.anchor: فيه إخوته أن يذهبوا بقميصه إلى أبيه فيلقوه على وجهه ليشفي الله به عينيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly turns the brothers' and Egyptians' attempts to lower Joseph into means of his rise: the pit and sale lead to Egypt, seduction to vindication, prison to rule, and the bloodied shirt's grief to restored sight.
rows.anchor: اجتمعت الأسباب على خفضه وأراد الله سبحانه رفعه فكان ما أراد الله دون الذي توجهت إليه الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph orders Jacob's entire household, including descendants, to move from the countryside to Egypt.
rows.anchor: أمر منه بانتقال بيت يعقوب من يعقوب وأهله وبنيه وذراريه جميعا من البدو إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣalat means the caravan departed and became separated; tufannidūn derives from fanad, weakness of judgment. Jacob senses Joseph's scent and expects their meeting soon, asking others not to dismiss him as foolish.
rows.anchor: الفصل القطع والانقطاع والتفنيد تفعيل من الفند بفتحتين وهو ضعف الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here qadīm means earlier in time; the sons repeat their earlier accusation that their father is in manifest error, at the story's beginning and end.
rows.anchor: القديم مقابل الجديد والمراد به المتقدم وجودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports identify the woman who traveled to Egypt as Benjamin's mother and Joseph's maternal aunt, while the scripture's apparent sense and other reports make her Joseph and Benjamin's mother; the evidence does not decisively displace the reports.
rows.anchor: كون امرأة يعقوب التي سارت معه إلى مصر وهي أم بنيامين خالة يوسف لا أمه الحقيقية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports that Jacob smelled Joseph from Palestine when the caravan left Egypt, at a distance of ten miles.
rows.anchor: قال وجد يعقوب ريح يوسف حين فصلت من مصر وهو بفلسطين من مسيرة عشرة أميال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say Joseph's shirt came from Paradise, was worn by Abraham in the fire, passed through Isaac and Jacob, and was Joseph's amulet; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says they cannot be authenticated and their chains are weak.
rows.anchor: هذه أخبار لا سبيل لنا إلى تصحيحها مضافا إلى ما فيها من ضعف الأسناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related reports say Jacob's letter called Isaac the intended sacrifice, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī maintains, as argued in the previous volume, that the intended son was Ishmael.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في الجزء السابق من الكتاب أن الذبيح هو إسماعيل دون إسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī reports that Joseph's brothers were neither prophets nor righteous, pointing to their accusation that Jacob was in old error.
rows.anchor: أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أكان إخوة يوسف أنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Sunni reports and some weak Shia reports call the brothers prophets, the author rejects this as incompatible with prophetic impeccability established by scripture, Sunna, and reason.
rows.anchor: وهذه الروايات مدفوعة بما ثبت من طريق الكتاب والسنة والعقل من عصمة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic term al-asbāṭ does not specifically identify Joseph's brothers as prophets; it can refer generally to Israel's tribes, descended from Jacob.
rows.anchor: والأسباط تطلق على جميع الشعوب من بني إسرائيل الذي ينتهي نسبهم إلى يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Muslim says Jacob postponed asking forgiveness for his sons until the predawn of Friday night.
rows.anchor: وفي الفقيه بإسناده عن محمد بن مسلم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās say Jacob delayed his prayer until Friday night or predawn because predawn supplication is answered; the Prophet also calls dawn the best time to invoke God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph immediately forgave his brothers and sought forgiveness for them, whereas Jacob did not take that same immediate stance when his sight returned.
rows.anchor: ولقد أقبل يوسف عليه السلام على إخوته حين عرفوه بالفتوة والكرامة من غير أن يجبههم بأدنى ما يسوؤهم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: In the answer to Yahya ibn Aktham, Jacob and his sons bowed as obedience to God and a greeting to Joseph, just as the angels' bow to Adam was obedience to God and a greeting to Adam.
rows.anchor: فإنه لم يكن ليوسف وإنما كان ذلك من يعقوب وولده طاعة لله وتحية ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report appears to imply that Joseph also bowed with them in gratitude, based on his subsequent thanksgiving, but that implication is unclear.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الحديث أن يوسف أيضا سجد معهم كما سجدوا وقد استدل عليه بقول يوسف في شكره

rows.speaker: بعض الروايات
rows.claim: Some reports say prophecy continued among Jacob's descendants through Levi, who prevented the brothers from killing Joseph and later remained behind in Egypt rather than breach his pledge.
rows.anchor: أن الله سبحانه جعل النبوة من آل يعقوب في صلب لاوي وهو الذي منع إخوته عن قتل يوسف

rows.speaker: بعض الروايات
rows.claim: Several reports say Joseph married the former wife of al-ʿAzīz after the latter died during the famine years; the author says this might be God's reward for her truthful confession, if the report is sound.
rows.anchor: وذلك بعدما مات العزيز في خلال تلك السنين المجدبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph, Jacob's son and one of twelve brothers, was singled out by a childhood dream; Jacob warned him against telling his envious brothers, who plotted his death and settled on casting him into a well.
rows.anchor: فبشره وهو صغير برؤيا رآها كأن أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر ساجدة له فذكر ذلك لأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers cast Joseph into the well, then returned with a bloodstained shirt and a false story; Jacob recognized their scheme through divinely inspired insight and grieved for Joseph.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل ذلك الا بتفرس إلهي ألقي في روعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caravan drew Joseph from the well; his brothers sold him cheaply, but the Egyptian minister bought him and gave him an honored home, turning their attempt to erase his memory into a path to elevation.
rows.anchor: وهذا أول ما ظهر من لطيف عناية الله بيوسف وعزيز ولايته له حيث توسل إخوته بإلقائه في الجب وبيعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph grew in worship and purity until God chose him and gave him judgment and knowledge, as God does with the people of excellence.
rows.anchor: وعاش يوسف في بيت العزيز في أهنأ عيش حتى كبر وبلغ أشده ولم يزل تزكو نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph resisted al-ʿAzīz's wife's seduction; a child testified to his innocence, but she accused him anyway, and God cleared him through the torn shirt.
rows.anchor: واعتصم بعصمة إلهية وقال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the king had a troubling dream that others could not interpret, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and sought his interpretation.
rows.anchor: وعند ذلك ادكر الساقي يوسف وتعبيره لمنامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dream as seven productive years followed by famine, proposed storing surplus grain, and was appointed to Egypt's stores after the women and al-ʿAzīz's wife cleared him; prison thus led to kingship.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه السنين انتصب يوسف لمقام عزة مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's brothers came for grain without recognizing him; he arranged for Benjamin to return, hid the royal cup in his baggage, and detained him under their own stated rule for theft, while their eldest stayed behind because of his pledge to Jacob.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه ثم أمر بالقبض عليه واسترقه بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After further famine drove the brothers back to Egypt, Joseph revealed himself; he attributes their eventual reunion and vindication to God's favor and says that God does not waste the reward of those who fear Him and remain patient.
rows.anchor: إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph forgave his brothers without reproach, prayed for their forgiveness, and sent them to fetch Jacob and the whole family with his shirt.
rows.anchor: فقابلهم يوسف بالعفو والاستغفار وقال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob sensed Joseph's scent as the caravan departed, and the returning shirt restored his sight; he acknowledged knowledge from God and promised to ask forgiveness for his sons.
rows.anchor: ولما فصلت العير قال يعقوب لمن عنده من بنيه إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reunited his family in Egypt, seated his parents, and all eleven brothers bowed; this fulfilled his childhood dream, after which Joseph thanked God for his kingdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا يعقوب وامرأته وأحد عشر من ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian people loved Joseph for his beneficence, and he called them to the monotheistic religion of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: يدعوهم إلى دين التوحيد وملة آبائه إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Torah account, Joseph tells his brothers his sheaf dream, and their jealousy increases.
rows.anchor: وحلم يوسف حلما فأخبر إخوته فازدادوا أيضا بغضا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Torah account Joseph dreamed of sheaves and of sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing; Jacob rebuked him while keeping the matter in mind, and the brothers plotted to kill him before Reuben intervened.
rows.anchor: وقصه على أبيه وعلى إخوته فانتهره أبوه وقال له ما هذا الحلم الذي حلمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah's version has Judah propose selling Joseph; Midianite traders sell him to Ishmaelites for twenty silver pieces, and the brothers use a goat's blood on his coat to deceive Jacob, who mourns for many days.
rows.anchor: وباعوا يوسف للاسماعيليين بعشرين من الفضة فأتوا بيوسف إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah says Potiphar's wife repeatedly sought Joseph, framed him after he fled, and induced Potiphar to imprison him; God remained with Joseph, who gained the prison keeper's trust and charge over the prisoners.
rows.anchor: وأما يوسف فأنزل إلى مصر واشتراه فوطيفار خصي فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah summarizes the cupbearer's and baker's dreams and Joseph's accurate interpretations, including the cupbearer's restoration, the baker's execution, and the cupbearer's forgetting Joseph for two years.
rows.anchor: ثم ساقت التوراة قصة صاحبي السجن ورؤياهما ورؤيا فرعون مصر وملخصه أنهما كانا رئيس سقاة فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Torah version Pharaoh's dream foretold seven abundant years and seven famine years; Joseph advised storing one fifth of the harvest and was appointed to govern Egypt, where he managed both periods well.
rows.anchor: فالآن لينظر فرعون رجلا بصيرا وحكيما ويجعله على أرض مصر يفعل فرعون فيوكل نظارا على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah recounts Joseph's brothers' first journey: he accused them of spying, detained Simeon, returned their money, and required Benjamin's arrival; Jacob reluctantly agreed after Judah pledged to return him.
rows.anchor: ثم قالت التوراة ما ملخصه أنه لما عمت السنة أرض كنعان أمر يعقوب بنيه أن يهبطوا إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second journey Joseph welcomed Benjamin and returned the brothers' gifts and money, then planted his cup in Benjamin's sack; the brothers found it and returned to Joseph.
rows.anchor: وأخرج إليهم شمعون الرهين ثم أدخلهم على يوسف فسجدوا له وقدموا إليه هديتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Torah account the brothers return to Joseph after the cup is found; Judah pleads to take Benjamin's place because Jacob would die of grief if Benjamin failed to return.
rows.anchor: فتقدم إليه يهوذا وتضرع إليه واسترحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reveals himself, says God sent him ahead to preserve life, and summons Jacob's household to Egypt; the Torah says seventy people settled in Goshen, where Joseph supported them during famine and Jacob lived seventeen years.
rows.anchor: أنا يوسف أخوكم الذي بعتموه إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah says Joseph wept so loudly after revealing himself that the Egyptians and Pharaoh household heard him.
rows.anchor: فأطلق صوته بالبكاء فسمع المصريون وسمع بيت فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have long used varied systems to interpret dreams; the Qur'an recounts Abraham's dream of sacrificing his son and its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتنى بشأنها في القرآن الكريم كما حكى الله سبحانه فيه رؤيا إبراهيم في ابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also recounts Joseph's dream, his prison companions' dreams, and Pharaoh's dream.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما حكاه تعالى من رؤيا يوسف عليه السلام إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Moses' mother's inspiration to place him in the chest is counted as a dream in reports.
rows.anchor: ومنها رؤيا أم موسى قال تعالى إذ أوحينا إلى أمك ما يوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Quran statement that the vision shown to the Prophet was made a trial for people.
rows.anchor: وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: European natural scientists generally deny that dreams are real or scientifically connected to external events, while some psychologists study them; authentic dreams disclose future events or hidden facts in ways chance cannot explain.
rows.anchor: الباحثين من علماء الطبيعة من أوربا لا يرون لها حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone has encountered dreams that reveal hidden matters or future events, especially clear dreams requiring no interpretation; their correspondence to later events cannot be dismissed as coincidence.
rows.anchor: ما منا واحد إلا وقد شاهد من نفسه شيئا من الرؤى والمنامات دله على بعض الأمور الخفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreaming is a mental act involving imagination, which recombines stored sensory images; bodily conditions, temperament, and emotions shape many ordinary dreams.
rows.anchor: والمتخيلة من القوى الفعالة دائما ربما تدوم في عملها من جهة الأنباء الواردة عليها من ناحية الحس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naturalist critics correctly identify bodily and emotional causes that shape many dreams, but their account only shows that some dreams lack truth.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي ذكره منكروا حقيقة الرؤيا من علماء الطبيعة لا يزيد على تعداد هذه الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that every dream is unreal does not follow: some sound dreams reveal truths and have a real relation to external events.
rows.anchor: وهو غير المدعى وهو أن كل منام ليس ذا حقيقة فإن هناك منامات صالحة ورؤيا صادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every dream has causes and thus an interpretation, but causes vary: bodily or temperamental influences, chance circumstances, and preoccupations can produce dreams without foretelling external events.
rows.anchor: فقد ظهر مما بينا أن جميع الرؤى لا تخلو عن حقيقة بمعنى أن هذه الإدراكات المتنوعة المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relevant true dreams are those not caused by external bodily or accidental factors, nor internal dispositions, yet connected to external events and cosmic realities.
rows.anchor: وإنما البحث في نوع واحد من هذه المنامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because future or hidden events are absent from the dreamer's senses, the author proposes that the sleeping soul connects to their causes beyond the physical world.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل إن الارتباط إنما استقر بينها وبين النفس النائمة من جهة اتصال النفس بسبب الحادثة الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes the physical world of changing matter, the imaginal world of immaterial forms that causes physical events, and the intellectual world of universal truths that causes the imaginal realm.
rows.anchor: أن العوالم ثلاثة عالم الطبيعة وهو العالم الدنيوي الذي نعيش فيه والأشياء الموجودة فيها صور مادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul able to grasp intellectual realities may see universal causes directly; otherwise it represents them through familiar images, and a sound soul may perceive causes without alteration in a clear dream.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت النفس كاملة متمكنة من إدراك المجردات العقلية أدركتها واستحضرت أسباب الكائنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other true dreams use symbols or opposites, such as a crown for honor or darkness for ignorance; these require interpretation by returning each image to the reality first perceived.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي التي تحتاج إلى التعبير بردها إلى الأصل الذي هو المشهود الأولى للنفس كرد التاج إلى الفخار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Symbolic dreams divide into manageable transformations and tangled sequences of transformations; the latter are confused dreams that resist interpretation, unlike clear dreams and interpretable symbolic dreams.
rows.anchor: المنامات التي تصرفت فيها النفس بالحكاية والتمثيل

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: In an example, Ibn Sīrīn interprets a dream of sealing people's mouths and sexual organs with a ring as becoming a Ramadan caller whose adhān makes people fast.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا رأى في المنام أن بيده خاتما يختم به أفواه الناس وفروجهم فسأل ابن سيرين
